> **Generated — do not hand-edit this table.** Each row's source is
> `_registry/<DEF###>.row.md` (one file per defect); rebuild with
> `scripts/registers/gen_registers.py gen def`. See [How to add a defect](#how-to-add-a-defect).

The processed record of every **defect** — a thing that is broken or wrong versus the
spec. Two sources feed it:

- **User-reported** — filed in-app (`POST /v1/feedback/bug` → `bug_reports` table on
  melehost), triaged by [`/fix-bugs`](../../.claude/commands/fix-bugs.md). The DB is the
  intake queue; **this file is the processed record.** When a report is worked, it gets a
  `DEF###` here.
- **Prompt-reported** — a defect Saiful (or Claude) spots in a session with no in-app
  report behind it. No `bug_reports` row; still gets a `DEF###` here when processed.

Sibling register for *planned* change (new work, not fixes): [`../forward_planning/cr_list.md`](../forward_planning/cr_list.md).
Governance rationale: decision **D-058** in [`../initial_specs/11_decisions/decision_log.md`](../initial_specs/11_decisions/decision_log.md).

## How to add a defect

**This table is generated** — never edit it by hand. A shared monolithic table gets
*swept*: on the shared `main` checkout the second committer captures the whole index and
silently steals another track's uncommitted rows (the 2026-07-24 DEF095/096 incident —
[CR081](../forward_planning/CR081_registers_are_architect_write_only/CR081_registers_are_architect_write_only.md)).
One file per item removes the shared write entirely. Instead:

1. **The Architect mints the ID.** Ask for the next `DEF###` (zero-padded, sequential,
   never reused) — one minter avoids the ID-collision race. Pre-triage items use a
   topic-slug handle until the ID is assigned.
2. **The item's domain owner writes one row file** — `_registry/DEF###.row.md` containing
   that defect's single markdown table row (columns below). One file per item is a disjoint
   write-path, so two tracks never collide. **Source** is `bug:<short-id>` (first 8 chars of
   the `bug_reports.id` UUID) for user-reported, or `prompt` for prompt-reported.
3. **Regenerate + pathspec-commit:** `python scripts/registers/gen_registers.py gen def`,
   then `git commit -m "…" -- docs/defect/_registry/DEF###.row.md docs/defect/def_list.md`.
   Never bare `git commit` / `-am` / `git add -A` (those re-introduce the sweep).
4. Fix it on a branch; the fix commit carries `fix(bug:<short-id>): <summary> (AT:R<N> DEF###)`
   (user-reported) or `fix(<scope>): <summary> (AT:R<N> DEF###)` (prompt-reported). Update
   your row file's **Fix** hash + **Status** and regenerate.
5. For a defect needing its own root-cause / design write-up, create
   `docs/defect/DEF###_<snake_case_topic>/` and link it from the row.

**Status** mirrors the operational lifecycle: `resolved` · `wont_fix` · `closed` (fixed
out-of-band) · `open` (in the DB, not yet worked — not usually listed here until processed).

| DEF039 | 2026-07-09 | prompt | other | `reputation_events` has no DB partial-unique index on its `(user_id, event_type, ref_id)` dedup anchor — dedup is app-code-only (a SELECT-then-INSERT race), so concurrent same-ref awards can double-insert (defense-in-depth gap on a monetized currency). Fix: partial unique index (`WHERE ref_id IS NOT NULL`, since ref_id is nullable and award() only dedups when given one) on both the ORM model (`sqlite_where` too, for `create_all()`-backed tests) and migration 0015 for Postgres. `award()` now catches the resulting `IntegrityError` on the losing side of a race, rolls back, and returns 0 — same contract as the existing dedup-check hit. +1 regression test simulating the race (`test_reputation_service.py`). Migration verified via SQLAlchemy model load + the SQLite-parity test only — the Mac has no live Postgres to dry-run `alembic upgrade head` against (pre-existing repo constraint: the full chain already fails on SQLite at an earlier, unrelated Postgres-only migration); real verification happens at `/promote-to-alpha`. | resolved | — | AT:R54 |
| DEF040 | 2026-07-09 | prompt | other | Account merge mid-week re-keys `reputation_events` and sums lifetime `reputation` but does not recompute the adopter's current-week `league_members.points` — a mid-week claim can undercount current-week league standing (lifetime reputation stays correct). (CR004 audit round-1 finding F5) Root cause: the league-seat re-key (`_rekey_skipping_conflicts` on `LeagueMemberRow`, conflict_col=week) drops the orphan's seat outright whenever both sides already hold one for the current week — the common case — leaving the adopter's `points` frozen at its pre-merge value even though the orphan's `reputation_events` (re-keyed just above it) now belong to the adopter. Fix: after the reputation re-key, if the adopter holds a current-week seat, recompute its `points` as a full resync (`sum(reputation_events.points)` over the current ISO week's bounds via `league_service.week_end()`) rather than a delta — correct regardless of which side's seat survived. +1 regression test that fails at `3 == 11` without the fix. | resolved | — | AT:R54 |

| DEF049 | 2026-07-11 | prompt | other | Streak-milestone **credit double-grant under concurrency** (monetized currency). `reputation_service._grant_milestone` calls `award(…, always_record=True)` then grants credits (`user.credit_balance += credits` + `SubscriptionEventRow`) **unconditionally**, without checking whether *its* `award()` call actually wrote the guard row. After DEF039 added the partial-unique index + `IntegrityError`→rollback→return-0 to `award()`, the loser of a concurrent same-milestone race rolls its guard-row insert back yet **still grants credits** → a one-time double credit. Surfaced by the DEF039 audit (finding O1); pre-existing and orthogonal (before DEF039 the same double-credit occurred *plus* a duplicate guard row, so DEF039 is neutral-to-positive here — not a regression). **Naive gate on `award()>0` is wrong** — a legitimately cap-clipped milestone returns 0 with the guard row written and credits owed (the exact F1 case `always_record` exists for). Fix: opt-in `_raise_on_race` flag on `award()` — the milestone path passes it, so a race-loss raises instead of returning 0, and `_grant_milestone` skips the credit grant; all other callers keep the return-0 contract. +1 regression test. Agents default to reading it as a per-trade stop-distance budget, which makes any name with a wide technical stop un-buyable regardless of sizing. This is not the safety floor working as designed — the floor is a portfolio constraint, and the Room is applying it as a position constraint. Suspected material contributor to the benchmark's 24% approve rate vs the Street's 63% buy rate. Note the sibling constraint from **DEF132**: `watcher.sh state` currently exits **1** on a successful read, so any liveness check that gates on its exit code inherits an inverted signal and must be built after (or alongside) that fix. NO <ROLE> WATCHER` line and `dispatch.sh inbox` exits 1 on it, putting the signal on the Architect's per-work-unit gate. **Absence is deliberately NOT an alarm**: an auditor spawned per item is told not to watch, so no-heartbeat is normal under that model and alarming on it would be permanently red — the CR099 alarm-fatigue rule. **TERM and KILL are deliberately not trapped**: a teardown-killed watcher is exactly the failure being caught, and cleaning up on the way out would erase the evidence; INT is trapped because a human pressing ctrl-C already knows. | DEF138 | 2026-07-28 | infra | governance | **The `/promote-to-alpha` hold gate matched `^### ` across the whole of `infra/PROMOTION_HOLD.md`, so the moment any hold was *cleared* — and its record kept in the file — the gate would have stayed shut forever.** Found while clearing the CR090-ROOM hold (the first clear since the gate shipped at AT:R65, `trail.md:80`), i.e. the defect was latent from the day the gate was written and could only surface on first use. The gate was `if grep -q '^### ' infra/PROMOTION_HOLD.md; then … exit 1; fi` — an h3 **anywhere** in the file counted as an active hold, including a cleared-hold history entry, a "how to raise a hold" example, or any future documentation subheading. **Measured, not reasoned:** with the CR090-ROOM block moved under a `## CLEARED HOLDS` section, the old gate still printed `PROMOTION HOLD ACTIVE — aborting. Holds: ### CR090-ROOM …` and exited 1. **The failure direction is the deceptive part.** It fails *closed*, which reads as safe — but a gate that can never open is a gate the operator learns to reason past, and `/promote-to-alpha`'s own text says *"do not reason your way past it."* A permanently-stuck fail-closed gate destroys exactly the authority the gate exists to have; the second time an operator overrides it, the hold mechanism is decoration. That is the **CR040 degrade-loudly** rule read from the other end: a control that cries wolf is not a control. It is also the same **allowlist/pattern-instead-of-invariant** shape that produced findings on CR104 rounds 1–2 and DEF120 rounds 1–2 — the gate pattern-matched on markdown syntax rather than on *"is there an entry under ACTIVE HOLDS"*, which is the actual invariant. **Fix (AT:R65):** the grep is scoped to the `## ACTIVE HOLDS` section with `awk '/^## ACTIVE HOLDS/{a=1;next} /^## /{a=0} a&&/^### /{print}'`, plus an explicit **fail-closed** branch when the file exists but has no `## ACTIVE HOLDS` heading at all — so deleting or renaming the section aborts promotion instead of silently opening the gate, which is the one mutation the scoping change could otherwise have introduced. Verified in all four states before commit: cleared-hold history present + none active → **exit 0**; a hold injected under ACTIVE HOLDS → **exit 1, hold printed**; the section heading removed → **exit 1, MALFORMED**; and the old gate against the same file → **exit 1**, which is the reproduction. Relates to **CR090** (whose hold this was), **CR040** (degrade loudly), **CR038** (a comment is not a control — the gate exists precisely because a runbook note was judged insufficient), and `failure_patterns.md` P2. | resolved | [CR090_live_data_feed_paywall/](CR090_live_data_feed_paywall/) | AT:R65 |
| DEF139 | 2026-07-28 | mobile | api-client | **The client renders SSE `error` payloads raw while the backend now escapes them, so a multi-line error message shows a literal `\n` to the user.** Consequence of **DEF127**, disclosed by the lane that caused it rather than left to be found. DEF127 routed every SSE `data:` field through `app/api/sse.py`, which escapes `\` and `\n` so an exception message can no longer end its own event early or forge a new one. For `token` events that is invisible — `mobile/lib/services/api/api_client.dart` calls `unescapeSseText` on them and the round-trip is exact (DEF127's guard pins it against the shipped `0.1.0+56` decoder). For `error` events it is not: the client takes the payload verbatim at two places — `parseRoomSseEvent` returns `{'kind': 'error', 'message': data}`, and the Brief / 1-on-1 loops `throw Exception('Server error: $data')` — so nothing inverts the escape. **Severity is cosmetic and the direction is an improvement, which is why it is a separate low-priority row and not a DEF127 round-2:** before DEF127 a multi-line error was *truncated at its first line* and the actual cause was silently discarded; now the whole message arrives, just with `\n` visible as two characters. No information is lost and no forged event is possible. **Fix shape:** call the existing `unescapeSseText` on error payloads at the two client sites — the function is already exported and `@visibleForTesting`, so this is a one-line change per site plus a test asserting a two-line error renders as two lines. Worth doing in the same lane as any other `api_client.dart` work rather than on its own. **Do not "fix" it by unescaping on the backend** — that would reinstate the framing hole DEF127 closed. Relates to **DEF127** (the fix that caused it), **DEF114** (the decoder this reuses), and **CR040**. | open | [DEF114_room_sse_parser_untested_paths/](DEF114_room_sse_parser_untested_paths/) | AT:R65 |
